reason: E2 demonstrates that phase inversion from a continuous ordered B2 matrix to a disordered BCC matrix with discrete ordered precipitates improves compressive ductility in a different alloy (Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr), supporting the general mechanism. However, no cited evidence addresses HfZrTiTa0.53 specifically, the proposed heat treatment parameters, tensile (rather than compressive) ductility, or the quantitative predictions for yield strength and uniform elongation.
premises: A continuous ordered B2 phase causes brittleness in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Phase inversion to a disordered BCC matrix with discrete ordered precipitates substantially increases ductility.
The proposed two-step heat treatment (1400°C/20 min + 600°C/120 h) will produce this phase inversion in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The phase inversion will increase room-temperature tensile uniform elongation from 13.5% to ≥20%.
Yield strength will remain within ±10% of 786 MPa after the heat treatment.
